Public open source repository
context: User originally chose private local, but later changed to public open source.
rationale: To share skills with the community and enable collaboration.

decision: Directory structure: ai-worker-skills/ for own skills, import/ for imported, personal/ for private
context: Need to organize skills by source and visibility.
rationale: Clear separation; personal/ is gitignored for privacy; import/ has metadata for attribution.

decision: Naming convention: ai-worker-skills get prefix 'ai-worker-', imports keep original name
context: User wanted brand recognition for own skills and clarity.
rationale: Easy to identify sources in tool UI; imports preserve upstream identity.
scope: plugin.json name, SKILL.md display name, marketplace.json entries

decision: Use Claude Code local marketplace via extraKnownMarketplaces
context: Need a standard way to install skills.
rationale: Native support; no extra scripts for Claude; OpenCode uses separate symlink approach.
alternatives_rejected: Custom install script for each tool

decision: skill-import skill behavior: fetch, extract, write metadata, register in marketplace
context: Automate import of third-party skills with proper attribution.
rationale: Ensure license compliance and traceability; reusable workflow.
scope: skill-import skill, import/ directory, META.yaml, plugin.json

decision: META.yaml schema with source, upstream_commit, license, imported_at, imported_by, note
context: Need structured metadata for each import for compliance.
rationale: Standard format; easy to validate in CI; human-readable.

decision: CI workflow to validate import metadata completeness
context: Ensure all imports meet attribution requirements.

decision: Test flat vs nested SKILL.md structure
rationale: Validate compatibility with Claude Code marketplace; both passed, so may adopt flat structure for simplicity.

decision: OpenCode installation: git plugin + project-level symlink
context: OpenCode does not support marketplace natively.
rationale: Git plugin offers easy sharing; symlink for per-project control.

decision: Personal skills symlinked directly, gitignored, not in marketplace
context: User wants private skills not exposed in public repo.
rationale: Privacy; simplifies git management; still usable via symlink.

decision: Add 'variant': 'thinking-high' to the build agent in opencode config
context: User requested to change thinking effort
rationale: Thinking effort is controlled via variant field; existing config had no variant for build agent, so added thinking-high variant

decision: 重建三个平级的 skill 目录：walter-worker-skills、import-skills、personal-skills
context: 原仓库结构混乱，用户明确要求三个独立目录存放不同来源的技能
rationale: 分离原生、导入和个人技能，便于管理和前缀规则实施
alternatives_rejected: 原先的 walter-worker-skills/import/ 子目录
scope: 仓库目录结构及所有 SKILL.md 中的路径引用

decision: walter-worker-skills 和 personal-skills 下的 skill 在 name 字段加 walter-worker- 前缀，文件夹名不改；import-skills 不加前缀；修改 CONVENTIONS.md 取消 name 必须匹配文件夹名的规则
context: 用户要求所有自身技能显示前缀，但文件夹保持原名
rationale: 满足显示需求同时避免大量文件夹重命名操作
alternatives_rejected: 仅在安装后修改显示名
scope: 三个 skill 的 SKILL.md 的 name 字段、CONVENTIONS.md、skill-create 的命名规则

decision: 在 skill-create 的 Phase 0 增加 GitHub 搜索（≥10 repo）和 Web 搜索，并提供 import/吸收灵感/自建三种决策分支
context: 用户希望 skill-create 能从外部获取启发，支持复用或借鉴
rationale: 增强技能创建时的外部参考能力，提升创建质量

decision: 在 ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md 添加规则：每次请求至少问1-3个 clarify 问题，除非置信度≥90%
context: 用户要求在所有任务中强制澄清需求
rationale: 减少误解，提高需求准确性；90%阈值避免过度打扰
scope: 全局 Claude 配置，影响所有项目

decision: 为 skill-import 增加 metadata.source_author 和 metadata.source_url 字段，并在 Quality Gates 中验证
context: 导入外部 skill 时需要保留原作者信息
rationale: 保证知识溯源，符合 open-source 规范
scope: skill-import/SKILL.md 的 frontmatter 及质量门禁

decision: 导入的 skill 放入独立的 import-skills/ 目录，而非 walter-worker-skills/import/
context: 用户明确要求三个平级目录，导入 skill 不应混合在工厂原生目录内
rationale: 保持目录职责清晰，避免混淆
scope: 目录结构、skill-import 的写入路径

decision: 保留并修复 skill-create 作为自举起点，而非从头重建
context: skill-create 是创建其他技能的入口工具，需要先修复问题再使用
rationale: 确保自举系统正确运行，避免重复工作
alternatives_rejected: 删除 skill-create 从零开始
scope: skill-create/SKILL.md 的问题修复及后续迭代

decision: Follow exact skill-create process phases (0->1->2->3->4) for skill-edit creation
context: User instructed to follow skill-create process exactly
rationale: Ensures consistency and quality enforcement across all skills

decision: Use provided requirements as user answers during interview (Phase 1)
context: User role simulated answers based on requirements
rationale: Simulate realistic interview without actual human interaction

decision: Accept default factor weights (Accuracy 0.4, Edge cases 0.3, Readability 0.15, Speed 0.1, Tool integration 0.05)
context: AI asked if user accepts defaults; user answered yes

decision: Build SKILL.md following opencode 5-field frontmatter format and CONVENTIONS.md body structure with target <150 lines
Include anti-patterns section in SKILL.md
context: Phase 2, instruction to include anti-patterns section, philosophy-driven approach

decision: Include quality gates section that blocks if violated (MUST gates)
Present diff summary and get user approval before editing (Step 4)
Use Edit tool for targeted changes, never Write on entire file, never create new file
rationale: Prevent overwriting or creating new files (skill-create's job)

decision: Run quality gates before commit; MUST gates block publish
Use conventional commit message format: skill(<name>): <imperative verb> <description>
Output only final SKILL.md content at end, not actually create files or commit
Redirect to skill-create if target skill doesn't exist or change is ≥80% rewrite
alternatives_rejected: Attempting to edit non-existent skill or full rewrite

decision: Skip interview phase and go directly to build with pre-specified requirements
context: User instructed to skip Phase 1 interview and proceed to Phase 2 build using provided requirements.
rationale: Requirements were complete, no need for elicitation.
alternatives_rejected: Conducting the interview phase to gather more details

decision: Use webfetch (preferred) or curl to fetch source SKILL.md
rationale: webfetch is more integrated; curl is fallback.

decision: Auto-convert frontmatter: map name to kebab-case, rewrite description to start with 'Use when...', default license to MIT, default compatibility to 'opencode, claude-code', infer triggers from description and body
rationale: Standardize all skills to opencode 5-field format with consistent defaults.

decision: Auto-adapt body sections: map Philosophy→overview, Anti-Pattern→Anti-Patterns, Workflow→Process, Checklist→Quality Gates; remove Changelog and Convention Notes
context: Body section mapping required to match CONVENTIONS.md structure.
rationale: All imported skills must follow the same structure for consistency and AI readability.
alternatives_rejected: Adding more mappings without user input

decision: Implement Ambiguity Triggers: ask user one question at a time only when mapping is ambiguous (no license, unclear triggers, unknown body section)
context: User requirement: ask ONE QUESTION AT A TIME only when ambiguous.
rationale: Minimize interruptions while ensuring correctness for edge cases.
alternatives_rejected: Ask user to fill all gaps upfront

decision: Define Quality Gates as MUST (block commit) and NICE (warn only) checklists
context: Quality section required by build instructions.
rationale: Ensure accuracy and compliance; separate blocking from non-blocking checks.

decision: Include Anti-Patterns section with four specific anti-patterns
context: Required by build instructions to have anti-patterns section.
rationale: Prevent common mistakes during import (silent conversion, verbatim copy, skipped audit, write to existing dir).

decision: Target <150 lines but accept 186 lines due to required content (conversion table, gates, anti-patterns)
context: User requirement 'Target < 150 lines'; output ended at 186.
rationale: Content completeness prioritized over strict line count; line count is soft target.
alternatives_rejected: Cutting required sections to meet line target

decision: Tighten NICE gate 'Body < 500 lines' to '< 150 lines' in skill-create
context: Diagnosis of skill-create revealed the body line limit was too loose per CONVENTIONS.md requirement.
rationale: CONVENTIONS.md specifies body should be under 150 lines; the existing 500-line limit would allow overly long skills.

decision: Add 'Anti-Patterns section present' as NICE gate in skill-create
context: skill-create lacked a requirement for an Anti-Patterns section, though downstream skills need it.
rationale: Ensures generated skills include anti-patterns, aligning with CONVENTIONS.md.

decision: Add 'Quality Gates section with MUST/NICE checkboxes' as NICE gate in skill-create
context: skill-create did not require a Quality Gates section in generated skills.
rationale: Makes quality criteria explicit and traceable, improving skill consistency.

decision: Add 'Philosophy-driven overview' as NICE requirement in skill-create Phase 2
context: Phase 2 instructions in skill-create were missing guidance to include a philosophy-driven overview.
rationale: Philosophical framing improves skill cohesion and user understanding.

decision: Add 'No deploy/ concept' prohibition as MUST gate in skill-create
context: CONVENTIONS.md prohibits deploy/ concept, but skill-create didn't check for it.
rationale: Prevents invalid skill structures from being created.

decision: Add 'description ≤ 500 chars' as NICE gate in skill-create
context: CONVENTIONS.md recommends description length ≤500 characters, but skill-create didn't enforce it.

decision: Accept Agent-B's assessment that skill-edit and skill-import have zero MUST violations
context: Double-checked both skills against CONVENTIONS.md and found no issues.
rationale: Both skills pass all quality gates; no additional issues found.

decision: Commit changes to skill-create and report with specific commit message
rationale: Follow standard development workflow for traceability.

decision: Use main agent orchestration with stateless subagents for each round (con, pro, judge) in devil-advocate skill.
rationale: Clear state management, debuggable, follows project's existing pattern (Agent-A/B/C bootstrap).
alternatives_rejected: Persistent sessions with task_id for cross-round memory (Scheme B) - risk of state drift and debugging difficulty.

decision: Change output path for devil-advocate from project default to {project-path}/docs/devil-advocate/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>/.
context: User requested a specific location (docs/devil-advocate) instead of docs/superpowers/devil-advocate.

decision: Create two output files for devil-advocate: discussion.md (full debate) and report.md (summary).
context: User asked '有没有discussion.md' (is there a discussion.md?).
rationale: Separate raw debate from human-readable summary.

decision: Limit debate to max 5 rounds, then fall back to 3-agent majority vote on unresolved points.
rationale: Prevent infinite loops; voting provides tie-breaker.
alternatives_rejected: No limit or different round count.

decision: Use triggers 'review spec', '杠精', 'devil advocate', 'adversarial review' for devil-advocate skill.
Use sequential two-agent architecture (Collector then Reviewer) without auto-retry for work-review skill.
rationale: Simple, clear separation of concerns; user manually re-triggers after fixes.
alternatives_rejected: Cyclic review with automatic re-check (Scheme B) - risk of infinite loop and skill responsibility creep.

decision: Agent 1 (Collector) writes a test plan (scenarios, types, steps) but no executable test code.
context: User corrected that Agent 1 should not write test code, only test plan.
rationale: Keep Agent 1's role limited to analysis and specification; Agent 2 executes.

decision: Agent 2 (Reviewer) executes the test plan by running existing UT/FT, writing Playwright for E2E, and using curl/httpie for manual tests.
context: User specified that Agent 2 should actually run tests, possibly write code, and use Playwright/dev's tests.
rationale: Agent 2 validates each acceptance criterion through real execution.
alternatives_rejected: Agent 2 only analyzing code without running tests.

decision: Output for work-review goes to {project-path}/docs/work-review/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>/ with acceptance.md and report.md.
rationale: Consistent with devil-advocate pattern, easy to find.
scope: Work-review output location and file structure.

decision: Use triggers 'work review', 'acceptance', 'sign off', 'verify work' for work-review skill.
Compress SKILL.md to under 150 lines to pass quality gate.
context: After writing devil-advocate SKILL.md, it was 271 lines, then reduced to 175, then 155.
rationale: Line count limit (NICE: 150) enforced by project guidelines.
alternatives_rejected: Leaving as is and ignoring quality gate.
